message: --- Q1. Differentiate between chgrp, chmod, and chown commands in Linux. (5 Marks) Command	Purpose	Example chgrp	Changes the group ownership of a file or directory.	chgrp staff file.txt chmod	Changes the permissions (read, write, execute) of a file or directory.	chmod 755 file.txt chown	Changes the owner (and optionally the group) of a file or directory.	chown ali file.txt Easy Trick chgrp → Change Group chmod → Change Mode (Permissions) chown → Change Owner --- Q2. Write 5 Postfix commands used in Linux. (5 Marks) systemctl status postfix systemctl start postfix systemctl stop postfix systemctl restart postfix postconf mail_version --- Q3. Explain the installation steps of a Kerberos Server on Ubuntu. (5 Marks) Step 1 Update Ubuntu packages. sudo apt update Step 2 Install the Kerberos server. sudo apt install krb5-kdc krb5-admin-server Step 3 Configure the Kerberos realm (e.g., VUSNA.COM). Step 4 Initialize the Kerberos database. sudo krb5_newrealm Step 5 Start the Kerberos services. sudo systemctl start krb5-kdc sudo systemctl start krb5-admin-server Step 6 Enable the services to start automatically. sudo systemctl enable krb5-kdc sudo systemctl enable krb5-admin-server Step 7 Create a principal. kadmin.local addprinc username Step 8 Verify the principal. listprincs --- Q4. Write the output/effect of the following command. (5 Marks) sudo install -m 077 -d /etc/apt/keyrings Explanation sudo → Runs the command with administrator (root) privileges. install → Creates files or directories. -m 077 → Sets the directory permission to 077 (Owner, Group, and Others all have read, write, and execute permissions according to the specified mode). -d → Creates a directory. /etc/apt/keyrings → The directory to be created. Output/Effect > Creates the /etc/apt/keyrings directory (if it does not already exist) and applies 077 permissions using administrator privileges. --- ⭐ Quick Revision chgrp → Change group chmod → Change permissions chown → Change owner 5 Postfix commands → status, start, stop, restart, postconf mail_version Kerberos installation → Update → Install → Configure realm → Create database → Start services → Create principal sudo install -m 077 -d /etc/apt/keyrings → Creates the directory with the specified permissions.
